correctness.rationale: For every positive integer the deficit is exactly the binomial mass of nonprimitive columns minus a reduced replacement mass bounded by \((n+1)2^{-n/2}\). The centered indicator of multiples of any positive integer has bounded partial sums; summation by parts against binomial unimodality gives uniform modular discrepancy at most twice the largest binomial mass. Möbius inversion therefore yields the asserted totient-profile inequality. Standard central-binomial and divisor bounds make the error tend to zero; summing the divisor estimate and the classical totient mean proves the quantified Cesàro limit. The prime and primorial cases are proved separately. Exact finite checks through index 320 are corroborative only.
